payload.title: welcome banner shows the correct signed-in user's name
payload.errorMessage:
expect(locator).toHaveText(expected) failed

Locator: getByTestId('welcome-banner')
Expected: "Welcome, Priya"
Received: "Welcome, Alex"

retries.errorHead:
expect(locator).toHaveText(expected) failed

Locator: getByTestId('welcome-banner')
Expected: "Welcome, Priya"
Received: "Welcome, Sam"

note: A wrong username in a welcome banner reads like a serious session-mixup bug, not a flake. But the two failed attempts land on two different wrong names — 'Alex', then 'Sam' — not the same wrong value repeating. A genuine session-mixup bug would consistently surface whichever specific stale session got cached, the same wrong name every attempt; landing on a different wrong name each time is the signature of a client-side session-cache read racing the fresh-login response and picking up whatever test worker's leftover session happens to be resident at that instant, not a deterministic defect. A one-shot read alone would call this REAL_BUG and could trigger a false security-adjacent alarm.
